nodes.description: Address with admin privileges; updated in constructor and acceptAdmin, read by onlyAdmin.
Pending admin address set via setPendingAdmin and consumed by acceptAdmin.
Cool-off delay in seconds, bounded by MIN_DELAY/MAX_DELAY, read in queueTransaction.
Mapping(bytes32 => bool) tracking queued/executed/cancelled transaction hashes.
Immutable constants MIN_DELAY, MAX_DELAY and GRACE_PERIOD that bound delay and execution windows.
Initializes admin from msg.sender and delay after bounds checks.
Payable receive hook allowing ETH transfers into the timelock.
Modifier requiring msg.sender == address(this); guards self-governed parameter changes.
Modifier requiring msg.sender == admin; guards privileged entry points.
onlyAdmin function that writes the pendingAdmin transfer target.
Two-step ownership transfer completion; sets admin = msg.sender when caller is pendingAdmin.
onlyTimeLock function that updates the delay with MIN/MAX bounds.
Private pure helper computing keccak256(abi.encode(target,value,signature,data,eta)).
External pure view of the transaction hash computed by _getTxHash.
onlyAdmin function that validates eta >= block.timestamp + delay and marks the hash queued.
onlyAdmin function that clears the queued flag for a known queued hash.
onlyAdmin payable function that clears the queue flag and performs an arbitrary low-level call after timestamp window checks.
Caller-controlled address used for admin assignment and all access-control checks.
Miner-influenceable timestamp used as eta bound and execution window bound.
Low-level target.call{value: value}(callData) forwarding arbitrary calldata and ETH to a user-supplied address.
Constructor delay argument checked against MIN_DELAY/MAX_DELAY and stored in delay.
Address argument written to the pendingAdmin state variable.
New delay argument bounded by MIN_DELAY/MAX_DELAY before being stored.
Destination address hashed into txHash and stored in the queue.
Earliest execution timestamp compared against block.timestamp + delay.
Arbitrary callee address used as the receiver of the low-level call.
ETH amount forwarded to the low-level call.
Queued execution timestamp checked against block.timestamp and GRACE_PERIOD.
Locally computed hash used as the queuedTransactions key and cleared before the call.
Payload assembled from signature selector plus data and passed to the low-level call.
Boolean result of the low-level call checked by require(success).
Bytes returned by the low-level call and forwarded to the caller.

edges.reason: Constructor assigns admin = msg.sender during deployment.
Untrusted msg.sender becomes the privileged admin account.
Constructor delay parameter is validated and consumed by the constructor.
Constructor delay parameter is written into the delay state variable.
MIN_DELAY/MAX_DELAY constants bound the constructor argument via require statements.
onlyAdmin modifier gates setPendingAdmin execution.
onlyAdmin compares untrusted msg.sender against admin.
admin state variable is read inside the onlyAdmin check.
setPendingAdmin argument is stored into pendingAdmin.
setPendingAdmin writes the pendingAdmin state variable.
acceptAdmin reads pendingAdmin to verify the caller.
acceptAdmin requires msg.sender == pendingAdmin before granting admin.
acceptAdmin reassigns the admin state variable to msg.sender.
onlyTimeLock modifier gates setDelay execution.
onlyTimeLock checks untrusted msg.sender against address(this).
setDelay argument is bounded and written to delay.
setDelay updates the delay state variable.
MIN_DELAY/MAX_DELAY constants bound the new delay value.
getTxHash delegates hash computation to the private _getTxHash helper.
queueTransaction computes the transaction hash via _getTxHash.
cancelTransaction computes the transaction hash via _getTxHash.
executeTransaction computes the transaction hash via _getTxHash.
onlyAdmin modifier gates queueTransaction.
onlyAdmin modifier gates cancelTransaction.
onlyAdmin modifier gates executeTransaction.
queueTransaction validates eta >= block.timestamp + delay, a timestamp dependency.
executeTransaction enforces block.timestamp >= eta and <= eta + GRACE_PERIOD.
delay state variable is read to compute the minimum eta.
queueTransaction target parameter flows into the queued hash.
queueTransaction eta parameter flows into the queued hash and timestamp check.
User-supplied eta is compared against block.timestamp.
queueTransaction sets queuedTransactions[txHash] = true.
cancelTransaction sets queuedTransactions[txHash] = false.
executeTransaction clears the queued flag before the external call.
executeTransaction requires the hash to be queued.
cancelTransaction requires the hash to be queued.
executeTransaction target parameter is hashed and used as the call destination.
executeTransaction value parameter participates in the tx hash and transfer.
executeTransaction eta parameter drives the timestamp window checks.
Locally computed txHash indexes the queuedTransactions mapping.
Assembled callData is forwarded verbatim to the low-level call.
User-supplied target address is the receiver of the low-level call.
User-supplied value is the ETH amount sent with the low-level call.
executeTransaction reaches an arbitrary external call on attacker-influenced target.
The callee can reenter executeTransaction (or other timelock entry points) during the external call.
require(success) branches on the low-level call result.
Low-level call return data is forwarded back to the caller.

normalization_plan.reason: Constructor delay parameter has no independent behavior; it is only bounded and stored by the constructor.
Parameter is a direct input of setPendingAdmin and is immediately written to pendingAdmin.
Parameter exists solely to be range-checked and assigned to delay inside setDelay.
Target is only consumed by queueTransaction's hash computation and queued accounting.
Eta is only consumed by queueTransaction's block.timestamp comparison and hash computation.
Target parameter directly becomes the receiver address of the unsafe low-level call.
Value parameter is forwarded as the ETH amount of the unsafe low-level call.
Eta is only used for executeTransaction's timestamp window requirements.
txHash is a transient local used only to key queuedTransactions within executeTransaction.
callData is built only to feed the unsafe low-level call payload.
success is a transient local checked immediately by require inside executeTransaction.
returnData is a transient local returned as the function result of executeTransaction.
